sections.html:
Springdale spreads across the Springfield Plateau in Northwest Arkansas and straddles the Washington and Benton county line. It was home to 84,161 people in 2020, fourth among Arkansas cities, and an estimated 90,685 in 2025.

Figure out your county before anything else. A parcel here sits in the Washington County system or the Benton County system, and the assessor, collector and recorder you will call change with the line. Tax dates and fees on this page describe Washington County parcels. A lot on the Benton side needs a call to that county's offices.

Just over half of homes are owner-occupied, so almost as many are rented. That means rental landlords and heirs holding a house with a tenant are a sizable part of the local seller pool. Treat the median value as a survey result and not as an appraisal of your house.

sections.h2: Selling a house with a tenant
sections.html:
Plenty of cash buyers will take a house with the tenant still inside, though the lease sets the pace. Read it for the end date and the rent before you commit, and be honest about how the tenant has paid. Pass along the tenant's contact details so an inspection can be scheduled.

An empty house is easier to show, but an empty rental earns nothing while you wait. Weigh that loss against what the buyer offers.

sections.h2: Which school district is your house in?
sections.html:
Almost the whole city is in Springdale Public Schools. The district also reaches Elm Springs, Tontitown, parts of Fayetteville, Goshen and Johnson in Washington County, and most of Springdale's Benton County side, including the former town of Bethel Heights.

Springdale annexed Bethel Heights on August 21, 2020. If you own a house there, make sure county and district records show the city boundary.

sections.h2: Sinkholes, storms and the ground under the house
sections.html:
Exposed Mississippian limestone underlies Springdale, and Washington County is full of springs, sinkholes and caves. The Boone Formation limestone beneath the plateau is known for solution and collapse sinkholes. Cracked walls, a settling slab or a dip in the yard will draw questions from a buyer's inspector. A cash buyer can purchase the house with that problem unsolved, and for some owners that settles the choice.

A tornado rated EF3 hit the city on March 30, 2022. Roof and siding claims are a usual part of a local house's history, so keep the insurance file and repair invoices in one place.

You can reach the Building Department at City Hall, 201 Spring Street, or by phone at 479-750-8114. The city site carries separate pages for building, planning, engineering and code enforcement. Staff can tell you which rules apply to your lot.

A seller can cover the basics before listing or taking an offer:

  • Ask the Building Department whether permits exist for a remodel, roof, deck or addition.
  • Ask Neighborhood Services if a complaint is open against the property.
  • Verify the parcel's county, because that tells you who collects the tax.
  • Pull together the deed, plus the lease and tenant contacts for a rental.

Washington County parcels owe tax by October 15. A late payment costs a 10 percent penalty, and real estate also gathers 10 percent annual interest. Statements are mailed each year, so if none has come by April 15, phone the collector at 479-444-1526.

Washington County began a four-year reappraisal cycle in 2023. A primary residence qualifies for a homestead credit of up to $600. Reappraisal can lift taxable value by no more than 5 percent a year on a homestead, and seniors and disabled owners can ask for a freeze.

Missing records cause most of the delays in a Springdale sale, so collect them early.

  1. Your deed, for the exact owner names and the legal description.
  2. This year's tax statement from whichever county bills the parcel.
  3. Permit records for any addition, deck or roof work.
  4. The lease and the tenant's phone number if the house is rented.
  5. Insurance and invoice records from tornado, roof or siding repairs.

If a piece is missing, the Building Department, the county assessor and the collector can each tell you what they hold for the address.

Unpaid tax does not prevent a sale, but it must be cleared at closing. Ask the collector for the precise balance, penalty and interest included. The title company then lists the payoff on the closing statement and pays it out of your proceeds, so the buyer gets a clean title.

If the sale will not close before the October 15 due date, ask the title company how the bill will be handled, since that is something to put in the contract. Keeping the paid receipt with your papers also saves a phone call later.

Waiting costs money because late real estate payments accrue interest each year. Learn the number now and you can set a cash offer beside a listing on honest terms.

A cash sale in Springdale follows a short path. The buyer reviews the property and your papers, then puts an offer in writing. You accept or negotiate, and a title company opens the file. The title company searches for liens, confirms who owns the house and which county taxes it, and prepares the closing statement.

On the closing date you sign the deed. Taxes, any mortgage payoff and recording costs come out of the proceeds. If the house has a tenant, the lease passes to the buyer, so the rent and deposit details should be settled in the contract.

If the house sits near the county line or in a recently annexed area such as Bethel Heights, tell the title company early. They will confirm the right county records and school district, which keeps a surprise from appearing late in the process.
Arkansas adds a transfer tax of $3.30 per $1,000 of the sale price. Put the payer in the contract, and ask the closing agent to confirm the figure.

Landlords with tenants in place, heirs living out of state and owners with deferred repairs are the usual fit for a cash sale. A well-kept house can bring more through a listing, so hear an agent out as well. Cash Home Buyers writes offers on houses as-is, with no number quoted until the property is understood.

To move quickly, have the deed, the latest tax bill, any lease and your list of known repairs ready. On closing day the title company settles any mortgage and tax balance from the proceeds and hands you the rest.

faqs.q: Is Springdale in Washington County or Benton County?
faqs.a: Both. The city crosses the county line, so look up your parcel to see which county assesses and bills it.

faqs.q: How many people live in Springdale, Arkansas?
faqs.a: An estimated 90,685 as of July 1, 2025, up from 84,161 in 2020. That 2020 figure ranked it fourth among Arkansas cities.

faqs.q: When is Washington County property tax due?
faqs.a: October 15. After that date real estate takes a 10 percent penalty and 10 percent annual interest.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Springdale rental with a tenant living in it?
faqs.a: Yes. Many cash buyers accept a tenant in place. Check the lease and agree on timing with the buyer before you sign.

faqs.q: Does a sinkhole or foundation problem stop a sale?
faqs.a: Not necessarily. A buyer will want an inspection and may lower the price, while a cash buyer can take the house as-is.
